4-b.decision_correctness_justification: The AI keeps the provided motion-energy trace, aligns it to imaging frames via timestamps, interpolates missing frames, and then bins it before categorization. This is at least as faithful as the reference and more robust in the presence of irregular or multiple dropped frames because it reconstructs alignment from the full timestamp sequence.

That is more robust than the reference implementation, which only uses percentile thresholds and assumes ties will not collapse categories.
4-c.code_correctness_justification: The code computes session-specific quantiles, applies `np.digitize`, and falls back to stable equal-count rank assignment when necessary.

4-d.decision_correctness_justification: The reference aligns motion to neural data by detecting dropped frames from interframe intervals and inserting interpolated values. The AI instead uses the full timestamp sequence, keeps one-to-one mapping when lengths already match, reconstructs frame indices over the full session span when they do not, and then bins/splits motion and neural data together. That is a more principled alignment strategy for the same problem.
4-d.code_correctness_justification: The alignment behavior described above is implemented in `align_motion_to_imaging()` and then carried through to the common binning and trial-splitting code.
